d.a: Distribution and ecological information: — The taxon was recently described despite its presence in Brazilian literature being misidentified as A. catenatum. Indeed, in our samples, the species A. tropicocatenatum had the highest frequency of occurrence (61 %). Its ecological optimum was calculated for all habitats. The species showed an ecological preference for slightly acid to neutral (pH optimum of 6.7 – 6.9), low to medium cond. (optimum of 53.7 – 94.3 μS ∙ cm- 1) and mesotrophic waters (TP optimum of 19.8 – 37.3 μg ∙ L- 1 and TN optimum of 504.2 – 665.8 μg ∙ L- 1). Achnanthidium tropicocatenatum was previously described from oligotrophic conditions in São Paulo state (Marquardt et al. 2017); however, it presented greater tolerance in our study area and was identified from oligo- to eutrophic conditions.
